content.text:
Plugins are still supported in v4, but the docs here don't cover how to write one.

- **Loading plugins:** use the `@plugin` directive. For example, `@plugin "@tailwindcss/typography";` accepts a package name or a local path. The docs call these "legacy JavaScript-based plugins" (`src/docs/functions-and-directives.mdx`, section "@plugin directive", around lines 296–306).
- **Mixing with CSS config:** `@plugin` and `@config` work alongside `@theme` and `@utility`. Things defined in CSS take precedence over those from plugins and configs (same file, around line 280).
- **Writing a plugin:** I found no page for the plugin API (`addUtilities`, `matchUtilities` and so on) in these docs. The v3 docs page isn't reproduced here, so I can't say from this material whether the v3 API is unchanged.

Plugins are still supported in v4, but the docs here don't cover how to write one.

- **Loading plugins:** use the `@plugin` directive. For example, `@plugin "@tailwindcss/typography";` accepts a package name or a local path. The docs call these "legacy JavaScript-based plugins" (`src/docs/functions-and-directives.mdx`, section "@plugin directive", around lines 296–306).
- **Mixing with CSS config:** `@plugin` and `@config` work alongside `@theme` and `@utility`. Things defined in CSS take precedence over those from plugins and configs (same file, around line 280).
- **Writing a plugin:** I found no page for the plugin API (`addUtilities`, `matchUtilities` and so on) in these docs. The v3 docs page isn't reproduced here, so I can't say from this material whether the v3 API is unchanged.
